title: How Do Old Trees Get Thicker? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
An old tree trunk gets thicker every year, even though its cells stopped dividing long ago. Diya asks: how does it keep growing, and how does a plant cell decide what to become?

We watch a cell differentiate into a tracheary element, zoom from a stem to a vascular bundle to one xylem cell, and follow step by step how parenchyma dedifferentiates into interfascicular and cork cambium and how new cells redifferentiate into wood. Then open differentiation at the root tip, development as one cell's story, and plasticity in larkspur and buttercup with a pause and think, a worked example naming each process, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 92 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
